Standardised precipitation indices before each interview, in one call

Source: R/wrappers.R
climate_indices.Rd

Runs the chain from a survey and a precipitation raster to one row per household and lag: the mean SPI (or SPEI) at each scale over the window before the interview, and the number of months below each drought threshold. Daily data are summed to months first. With pet, the SPEI is computed from the water balance.

Usage

climate_indices(
  survey,
  pre,
  pet = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  interview = NULL,
  preset = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  below = NULL,
  above = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  boundaries = NULL,
  control = indices_control()
)

Arguments

survey

The survey: a data frame with coordinates, a household identifier and interview dates, or a table from prepare_coord(); or a named list of them.

pre

Monthly (or daily) precipitation: a file path, a SpatRaster or an extracted table.

pet

Optional potential evapotranspiration, the same way; switches to the SPEI.

lat, lon, id, interview

<tidy-select> Survey columns: coordinates (found by name when left out), household identifier and interview date. Not needed after prepare_coord().

preset

Name of a preset, e.g. "heat" or "wet_days_p95".

index

"spi" or "spei"; by default SPEI when pet is given.

scale

Accumulation scales in months; default c(1, 3, 6).

below, above

Thresholds on the index; default below = c(-1, -1.5, -2).

window

The reference window; default the month before the interview.

boundaries

Optional administrative divisions: indicators are then computed per cell and averaged per division (area shares).

control

Further options, see indices_control().

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per household and lag.

Details

The chain: prepare_coord(), georef_coord(), read_climate(), aggregate_time() when daily, extract_by_coord() (or cells and aggregate_to_adm() with boundaries), calc_std_index(), calc_std_threshold() and summarise_by_interview().

See also

weather_extremes(), list_presets()

Examples

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)

climate_indices(survey,
                system.file("extdata", "pre_monthly.tif", package = "c4e"),
                id = hhid, interview = interview, scale = 3)
#> Using lat as `lat`.
#> Using lon as `lon`.
#> Taking the coordinates as longitude and latitude in "EPSG:4326"; give `crs`
#> otherwise.
#> Read pre_monthly: pre [mm/month], monthly, 1984-01-01 to 2023-12-01, 480 layers
#> (synthetic).
